meta.note: Editorial use cases with one-line why per pick

useCases.title: Best research tools
useCases.summary: Web search and deep research for builders and agents.
useCases.audience: Builders researching markets, docs, and competitors — plus agents that need reliable search.

editorial.why: Best default for fast, cited answers without leaving the browser.
Neural search that returns pages agents can actually use.
Drop-in search API when your agent needs structured results.

useCases.title: Best AI coding editors
useCases.summary: Editors where vibe coding actually ships.
useCases.audience: Vibe coders and solo builders who live in the editor.

editorial.why: Still the sweet spot for AI-native editing and multi-file changes.
Cascade agent feels like a teammate inside a full IDE.
Blazing fast when you want AI without the bloat.

useCases.title: Best coding agents
useCases.summary: Agents that write, test, and iterate on code for you.
useCases.audience: Builders who want agents to take a ticket from prompt to PR.

editorial.why: Strongest terminal agent for real repos and long sessions.
Open, model-agnostic, and great for git-aware pair coding.
Closest to autonomous end-to-end engineering — when budget allows.

useCases.title: Best AI video tools
useCases.summary: Text-to-video and editing tools for demos and content.
useCases.audience: Builders shipping product demos, launch videos, and social clips.

editorial.why: Most polished creator workflow from prompt to edit.
Strong motion and longer clips for cinematic demos.
Fast iterations when you need volume over perfection.

useCases.title: Best MCP servers / agent tooling
useCases.summary: Connect agents to tools, browsers, and APIs.
useCases.audience: Agent builders wiring real-world actions into their stack.

editorial.why: The open standard — start here before picking vendors.
Hundreds of managed integrations so you skip OAuth hell.
Reliable headless browsers when agents need to click the web.

useCases.title: Best AI writing for builders
useCases.summary: Writing tools that help ship docs, threads, and product copy.
useCases.audience: Builders who need clear writing without a content team.

editorial.why: Best when your docs already live in Notion.
Purpose-built for shipping builder threads on X.
Quick polish for READMEs, emails, and landing pages.

useCases.title: Best agents for code review
useCases.summary: Catch bugs, style issues, and risky diffs before you merge.
useCases.audience: Builders who want agents to review PRs like a careful teammate.

editorial.why: Inline review in the editor where the diff already lives.
Strong on multi-file context and repo-aware critique.
Paste a diff or PR summary for careful, readable feedback.

useCases.title: Best scrape-to-brief workflows
useCases.summary: Pull pages into clean text, then turn them into a usable brief.
useCases.audience: Builders and agents researching competitors, docs, and markets.

editorial.why: Best default when you need agent-ready markdown from messy sites.
Use when the page needs a real browser before you can extract.
Fast at turning scraped notes into a structured brief.

useCases.title: Best meeting notes → tasks
useCases.summary: Turn calls into action items without rewriting everything by hand.
useCases.audience: Solo builders and small teams drowning in standups and customer calls.

editorial.why: Reliable transcripts plus action items straight from the call.
Best when tasks should land next to the rest of your docs.
Great at cleaning messy notes into owners, due dates, and next steps.

useCases.title: Best AI SEO draft tools
useCases.summary: Draft landing pages and long-tail posts that still sound human.
useCases.audience: Builders shipping content for organic discovery without a content team.

editorial.why: Fast outlines and drafts when you already know the keyword intent.
Stronger long-form tone control and fewer generic SEO clichés.
Cite live sources while you map angles and competing pages.

useCases.title: Best tools for game NPC prototyping
useCases.summary: Prototype conversational NPCs and character brains before full production.
useCases.audience: Indie game builders and vibe coders prototyping dialogue systems.

editorial.why: Purpose-built character brains with personality and memory hooks.
Quickest way to try dialogue loops before wiring a game engine.
Good for longer character bibles and consistent voice guides.

useCases.title: Best Discord bot ops with agents
useCases.summary: Build, wire, and operate Discord bots with agents and integrations.
useCases.audience: Community builders and vibe coders running Discord as product infrastructure.

editorial.why: Skip OAuth glue — connect Discord actions into your agent stack.
Best place to ship bot code and iterate on handlers fast.
Handy for longer bot refactors and test passes in the terminal.

useCases.title: Best PR → changelog agents
useCases.summary: Turn merged PRs into release notes humans actually want to read.
useCases.audience: Builders who ship often and hate writing changelogs from scratch.

editorial.why: Reads the repo and git history, then drafts release-ready notes.
Great for editing changelog drafts beside the actual PR diff.
Paste commit messages and get a clean user-facing summary fast.

useCases.title: Best browser QA for agents
useCases.summary: Automate click-paths and catch UI regressions before users do.
useCases.audience: Builders who want agents to smoke-test flows in a real browser.

editorial.why: Industry default for stable e2e tests agents can generate and run.
Hosted browsers when your agent needs cloud sessions, not local Chrome.
Write and fix Playwright specs in the same place you ship the app.
